safety.server.detail: This workspace is for review records, not clinical data. If patient information is entered by mistake, a project owner can purge it from the history; report it as your organization's policy requires.

access.title: Access
access.unenforced.title: Roles are not enforced in this view.
access.unenforced.detail: This browser has no signed-in user, so there is nobody to check a permission against. Anyone who can open this page can change anything in it. Run the tool with a backend, or publish it as a shared artifact, for access control to mean anything.
access.open: No access list recorded, so this project is open to everyone in the workspace. Claim it to restrict who can change it.
access.sole.title: You are this project's only owner.
access.sole.detail: If your account is disabled, for instance when you leave, nobody will be able to open, export or reassign this record, and it becomes unreachable. Add a second owner below.
access.lede: Owners can delete, archive and change access. Writers can fill in the review. Readers can see it and change nothing.
log.title: Changelog
log.lede: Every change to this record, with who made it and when.
log.cap: This view shows at most 500 entries. The full history is available from the API: {api}
fp.title: Record fingerprint
fp.lede: A fingerprint of this record's contents right now. Quote it alongside an exported report to tie the report to the exact state it came from. Volatile fields, such as the last-saved timestamp, are excluded so the fingerprint only moves when something substantive does.
fp.warnDetail: MD5 has been collision-broken since 2004, and anyone who can edit the record can also recompute its fingerprint. It answers "is this the same version?" and must not be offered as evidence that a record was not altered. A SHA-256 travels in the JSON export for anyone who needs the stronger property.
flag.noDeployDate: Live with no deployment date recorded at Checkpoint C
flag.retrain: Last review asked for retraining or revision
flag.noConditions: {gate}: conditional approval with no conditions recorded
flag.noRationale: {gate}: approved with open criteria and no rationale
stage.answered: {answered} of {total} answered. Give anything partial or not met an owner and a due date; overdue actions are flagged on the dashboard.
md.hint: Formatting: **bold**, *italic*, - or 1. for lists, [text](https://address) for links. No tables, images or HTML.
refs.title: Evidence references
refs.hint: A file is never uploaded: only its name, size and SHA-256 are kept, so anyone holding the file can check it is the one relied on. Do not put patient information in a title or a file name.
refs.badUrl: That address is not allowed. Use a full http or https link, without a username or password.
refs.needOne: Add a link, a file, or both.
refs.tooBig: That file is larger than {mb} MB.
refs.full: This item has the most references allowed.
refs.unreadable: That file could not be read.
refs.match: This is the same file: the SHA-256 matches.
refs.mismatch: This is not the same file: the SHA-256 differs.
metrics.title: Key metrics
metrics.lede: Report each metric with the population it was measured on. Add one row per subgroup for fairness results.
metrics.none: No metrics yet. Add the ones your team will stand behind.
te.choose: Choose a use case to see the methods and metrics CHAI's workgroups agreed on for it.
te.recommended: Recommended by CHAI for this use case
te.credit: {count} methods and metrics, reproduced under CC BY 4.0 from {link}, © 2025 Coalition for Health AI. Follow the link for each one's description, rationale, benchmark and supporting literature.
te.lede: CHAI's guidance is to review the use-case Testing & Evaluation framework when completing the model card. Selecting a metric adds its name and category; the value and population stay yours to measure.
te.note: These metric names are an unofficial, machine-drafted translation of CHAI's English names; the English original governs. The descriptions behind the link are in English, and a metric you add keeps CHAI's English name.

del.removes: This removes the review for everyone: the checklist, every checkpoint decision and its sign-offs, the model card and the live audit log, and it leaves the portfolio.
del.historyKeptDetail: Every earlier revision stays readable by owners, so the record can still be audited. That is usually what you want. To destroy that too, choose it below.
del.destroys: This destroys the review for everyone: the checklist, every checkpoint decision and its sign-offs, the model card and the audit log. It cannot be undone.
del.purgeChoice: Also permanently destroy its version history and the content of its audit log
del.purgeHint: For something that should never have been recorded, such as a patient identifier. It cannot be undone. Who changed what, and when, is kept; what was written is not. Backups made earlier still hold it.
del.archiveInstead: Archive it instead if you only want it off the active portfolio. Archiving keeps the whole record and can be reversed.
session.lockedDetail: This workspace locked after a period of inactivity, so the record is not left open on an unattended screen. Your changes were saved. Reload to continue; you may be asked to sign in again.
rules.title: This page and its server disagree about when records are retired.
rules.titleUnsynced: The server's retirement rules were not confirmed against this page.
rules.primary: The server retires records by the rules of the framework "{server}", but this page was built for "{page}". Ask whoever runs this server to run its migrate job with this build's manifest.json.
rules.hash: The server retires records by different rules than this page shows, so a decision recorded here could make a record due for disposal when this page says it is not, or the reverse. Ask whoever runs this server to run its migrate job with this build's manifest.json.
rules.unsynced: No build's manifest.json set or confirmed the rules the server retires records by. Ask whoever runs this server to run its migrate job with this build's manifest.json.
rules.blocked: Until they agree, this page records no decision and creates no new record.
rules.refused: Not saved: the server retires records by different rules than this page shows. See the notice at the top of the page.
report.readinessDetail: of applicable criteria met (partial counts as half, unanswered as zero). {answered} of {total} items answered
report.noGaps: No open gaps. Every applicable criterion is met.
report.disclaimer: This report organizes a local review around the Coalition for Health AI (CHAI) six-stage lifecycle and five principles, and the structure of the CHAI Applied Model Card. Checklist wording is a paraphrased summary, not the official CHAI Responsible AI Checklist. It is an internal governance record, not a certification, legal opinion, or regulatory determination.
label.foot: Structure follows the CHAI Applied Model Card template (draft v0.1). Prepared by the deploying organization; not a CHAI certification.
optica.paraphrase: Questions are this project's paraphrase of OPTICA, not its published wording.

optica.chipNote: The chip on each row names the CHAI criterion that partially covers it, or a dash where none does.
optica.title: Adoption review
optica.lede: 77 items in 13 chapters. OPTICA asks whether this organization should adopt this solution; it runs alongside the CHAI lifecycle and never changes it.
optica.relay: Outstanding items are listed by who can answer them: your organization, the solution's developer, or either party.
optica.neverTitle: OPTICA answers never change CHAI status.
optica.neverDetail: The two checklists ask different parties for different evidence at different moments, and no OPTICA item fully discharges a CHAI criterion. Evidence can be cited in both; a judgment in one is not a judgment in the other.
optica.off: OPTICA is not switched on for this project.
optica.turnOn: Turn it on in {setup} to add its 77 adoption questions alongside the CHAI lifecycle.
provenance.local: Kept in one browser on one computer. Sign-offs here are self-asserted: nothing verifies who made them, and there is no server-side audit log or version history.
provenance.api: Kept on the self-hosted governance server, with server-side access control, a version history and an audit log. Sign-offs are recorded against the signed-in identity.
provenance.unknown: The storage mode was not known when this was produced.
export.fingerprint: Record fingerprint (SHA-256): {sha256}. MD5: {md5}. It identifies this exact version of the record.
md.overall: Overall: **{pct}%** of applicable criteria met ({answered}/{total} answered).
md.footer: Structured around the CHAI six-stage lifecycle and Applied Model Card. Checklist wording is paraphrased; this is an internal governance record, not a CHAI certification.

hold.explainLift: Once lifted, this record can be disposed of when its retention period has passed. Confirm with counsel first.
hold.reasonHint: Kept with the hold and shown only to owners, not in the project's history.
